newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Caspian sees consumer-driven Argentine bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Caspian sees consumer-driven Argentine bolsa.

text.p: Argentina's stock exchange will be powered by higher consumption in 1997 and an expected 20 percent rise in loans to the private sector, Caspian Securities said Thursday in a report.

"We believe consumption will surge 4.8 percent during the year, backed by improved consumer confidence," Caspian said, giving a year-end target for the blue-chip MerVal index of 790, compared to 730 at Wednesday's close.
Caspian said it based this forecast on:
-- 13.6 percent growth in corporate earnings for 1998. -- low country risk.
-- strong demand from local pension funds for equities.

It singled out Banco Frances, Banco de Galicia, Irsa, Ciadea, Corcemar and Fiplasto as best buys based on economic growth, and Telefonica, Siderca, Capex and Transportadora Gas del Sur on fundamentals.

Caspian said the bolsa, trading at 14.4 times 1997 earnings, had a 28 percent premium to other Latin American markets, but its growth could be hampered by October's mid-term elections in Congress and campaigning for the presidency before 1999.
It also warned of a possible reversal of international liquidity conditions, thwarting capital flows, and of possible economic setbacks in Argentina's main trading partner Brazil.
-- Industrial production growth of 6.4 percent in 1997.
-- A current account deficit of 1.8 percent of gross domestic product in 1997 and 2.2 percent in 1998.
-- Central Bank reserves of $23 billion at the end-1997 and $24 billion at end-1998 due to expected capital inflows of 2.7 percent and 2.4 percent of GDP each year, respectively.
-- A primary fiscal deficit of $5.2 billion in 1997, only 1.6 percent of GDP versus 1.9 percent in 1996.
-- Inflation of 2.5 percent each in 1997 and 1998.
-- A trade deficit of $1.4 billion in 1997 and $2.7 billion in 1998.
